slides.headline: October 24, 1945: the United Nations Charter took effect - and India had already signed it, two years before its own independence.
October 24 marks UN Day, observed since the UN Charter entered into force in 1945
slides.body: India was a founding member of the United Nations, having signed the Charter at the San Francisco Conference in June 1945 - while still under British rule, more than two years before independence in August 1947.

slides.headline: India entered the world's premier international body before it had full control of its own government.
slides.body: India's UN membership traces back even further - to its signing of the 1942 Declaration by United Nations in Washington - giving the country an institutional seat at the global table years before it could set its own domestic policy.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat builds on an international standing that predates its own sovereignty.
slides.body: Having a seat at the UN's founding gave India a permanent voice in global institutions from day one - a head start few other newly independent nations had.
